project.name: Not Arbitrary 02 — Where Our Letters Came From

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Look at the letter A. It does not look like anything in particular. That is only because it has been turned upside down.
entries.direction: Warm, unhurried, opening a story. A small hook in the last sentence.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Around three thousand eight hundred years ago, in the Sinai desert, someone drew an ox head. Two horns, and a narrow face.
entries.direction: Conversational, as if sketching while speaking.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: They called it aleph, their word for ox. The picture stood for the sound that word began with. A drawing, doing the job of a letter.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The Phoenicians simplified it. The Greeks turned it over. The horns became legs, and the face became a point.
entries.direction: Three clear beats, one per step, slightly quickening.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: That is the letter A. Still an ox, standing on its head.
entries.direction: Quiet satisfaction. Let the last phrase sit.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The second letter was a house. A floor plan seen from above, with a doorway on one side.
entries.direction: Descriptive, tracing the shape with the voice.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Beth means house. Turn it upright, round off the corners, and you are looking at the letter B.
entries.direction: Matter of fact, with a lift on the final letter.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Water was a wave. Three crests, drawn in a single stroke.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: This one is worth stopping on. In China, the picture for water was a current with droplets flying off it. In the Sinai, it was a wave. Two systems that never met, reaching for the same picture.
entries.direction: Slower, a little wonder in it. The quiet centre of the film.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Stand that wave on its end, and it is M.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: And an eye. An outline, and a pupil in the middle of it.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The pupil fell away. The outline stayed, and became the letter O.
entries.direction: Three short beats, the last one settled.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: An ox, a house, water, and an eye. Four drawings. Four of the letters you use every single day.
entries.direction: Deliberate, one item at a time, like laying cards down.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: You have been reading pictures your entire life. They only stopped looking like anything about two and a half thousand years ago.
entries.direction: Warm close, slowing into the final line.
